messages:
karen_finance: Reseller flagged a weird negative line on their Azure Marketplace invoice — looks like a discount tier override applied twice, resulting in a refund line. Can someone sanity-check?

jose_partners: yikes. invoice id? reseller?

karen_finance: invoice INV-2027-01-12-chan-58, reseller channel-orchid, sub res-58. Invoice shows charges $2,700 and a credit -$1,800 labeled 'tier-discount override' resulting in net $900. Reseller says they only expected a single 30% partner discount on qualifying seats, not a double override.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2027-01-12-chan-58 created for $900.00 (gross $2,700.00 less discounts). Billing period: 2027-01-01 to 2027-01-31.

liam_billing: Can you paste the SKU/tier mapping and discount audit rows? need to see which rule fired twice.

karen_finance: paste (redacted):
2027-01-01T00:00:00Z,res-58,sku:pro,qty:100,base_rate:30
2027-01-01T00:00:00Z,discount_rule:partner-tier-30pct,applies_to:seat_range:1-100
2027-01-02T03:12:00Z,discount_rule:partner-tier-30pct,applies_to:seat_range:1-100,override:true

karen_finance: looks like an additional 'override' row was ingested on 1/2 that duplicates the original rule. Why did it reapply after snapshot?

liam_billing: suspect connector replay or partner issuing an override to retroactively change discount. If override.ingest_time > snapshot_time we shouldn't mutate finalized invoice. Check audit-log: whether discount mutations were allowed post-snapshot.

ingest-bot: Created ticket TCK-8122: "Marketplace discount override applied post-snapshot causing negative line - res-58" assigned to eng-ops.

jose_partners: pinging partner-ops — partner confirms they pushed an admin override on 2027-01-02 to correct mapping, but they expected it to apply to next billing cycle only. Their UI had a toggle 'apply retroactively' accidentally on.

liam_billing: finance policy: overrides with retroactive flag are allowed but must be gated and produce audit notice prior to invoice issuance. Here the invoice snapshot was 2027-01-01 00:00Z, so retroactive changes after that should not alter the already generated invoice; they should create a corrective credit/invoice pair. Looks like our pipeline applied override in-place.

karen_finance: finance prefers issuing a corrective credit/invoice rather than letting retroactive edits mutate an issued invoice. Propose: 1) void the credit line and create corrective invoice showing adjustment + memo, 2) create partner-facing note explaining policy, 3) require eng change to block in-place mutation after snapshot. Approve provisional adjustment up to $2k.

billing-bot: Action logged: TCK-8122 updated with finance provisional approval up to $2,000. AP payment hold placed.

liam_billing: I'll open a hotfix to prevent discount_rule.apply changes from editing historical invoice objects — instead emit delta entries into a pending corrections queue. Also add an alert if an override.ingest_time > snapshot_time and retroactive flag true.

jose_partners: partner accepts corrective invoice approach. They'll reconfigure their UI to default 'apply retroactively' off.

karen_finance: cool. I'll draft the corrective invoice & memo and attach to TCK-8122 once eng confirms the hotfix. Target EOD tomorrow.

liam_billing: noted. I'll assign eng-ops owner and update ticket with PR link when ready.

karen_finance: thanks all — lesson: treat discount overrides as immutable for issued invoices unless processed via corrections flow. :memo:

jose_partners: thanks team :thumbsup:
